title: Evaluating the Reliability of Online Content
kicker: تانية بكالوريا · Reading · Unit 3 · Unit 6 · Unit 7 · Unit 9
summary: إزاي تحكم على بوست أو خبر أونلاين: موثوق ولا مضلل؟ من لغته ومصدره وأدلته، باستخدام جدول الكتاب.

text: A **reliable** source gives information that is accurate, supported by evidence and written by someone who knows the topic. An **unreliable** (misleading) source uses emotion, exaggeration and pressure instead of evidence.

blocks.text: كل يوم بنشوف على السوشيال ميديا بوستات بتقول حاجات صادمة: «اكتشاف خطير»، «الحق قبل ما يتمسح»، «اكسب مليون في شهر». الدرس ده بيعلمك تسأل: **أصدّق البوست ده ولا لأ؟** وده اسمه **evaluating reliability** (تقييم المصداقية).

المهارة دي متكررة في الكتاب كتير، وكل مرة تحت عنوان **Social Media Post for Analysis**: في **Unit 3** (بوست عن «لمبات دندرة» والكهربا عند المصريين القدماء)، في **Unit 6** (بوست عن انهيار أعداد القروش)، في **Unit 7** (بوست «إزاي عملت براند بمليون دولار من أوضتي في 30 يوم»)، في **Unit 9** (بوست عن الانتماء والـ well-being)، وكمان في **Unit 10** (بوست موضة بيقول «100% sustainable»). الكتاب بيقولك: «Read this post carefully. You will analyze its language and **assess its reliability**».

والكتاب في المقدمة بيقول إن الـ **E** في JRE (Evidence) معناها إنك تدعم كلامك بـ «**reliable evidence**» وتعرف «distinguish **credible** sources from **unreliable** ones». يعني المهارة دي جزء من طريقة الكتاب كلها.

blocks.title: ملحوظة
blocks.text: كل البوستات اللي في الدرس ده **من تأليفنا للتدريب** (fictional) زي ما الكتاب بيعمل. الأسماء والحسابات مش حقيقية.

text: The book gives five features to look for: emotional language, absolute language, urgency signals, selective evidence and conspiracy framing.

headers: تدوّر على إيه (What to look for)
rows: words designed to provoke, excite or alarm

بيوريك جزء صغير من الصورة أو المعلومة ويخبي الباقي

blocks.title: حيلة للحفظ: EASSC
blocks.text: **E**motional – **A**bsolute – **S**elective – **S**ense of urgency – **C**onspiracy. لو البوست فيه 2 أو أكتر من دول، **وقف قبل ما تصدّق أو تعمل share**.

text: Language is not the only clue. Also ask: Who wrote it? What evidence is given? When was it posted? Why was it written? Do other reliable sources say the same?

rows: خبير، جامعة، متحف رسمي، صحفي معروف، اسم حقيقي
مصدر مذكور، دراسة، رابط لجهة رسمية، رأي خبير
«Scientists confirm» من غير ما يقول مين
يبيع حاجة، يجمع لايكات، «Link in bio»
مواقع موثوقة كتير بتقول نفس الكلام

blocks.title: فخوخ مشهورة
items: **عدد المتابعين أو اللايكات مش دليل**. بوست عليه 241,000 لايك ممكن يكون كله غلط. الانتشار ≠ الصدق.
**العلامة الزرقا (verified)** معناها إن الحساب صاحبه حقيقي، **مش** إن كل كلامه صح.
**صورة حقيقية** ممكن تتحط مع **كلام غلط** (selective evidence). نقوش دندرة حقيقية، لكن تفسيرها إنها «لمبات» تفسير غلط.
البوست **المتوازن** مش لازم يكون ممل: ممكن يكون مثير ومع ذلك يذكر المصدر ويقول «may» و«some».

text: THEY LIED TO YOU!!! The pyramids were NOT built by Egyptian workers. Every historian knows the truth but nobody dares to say it. This one photo PROVES everything. Share before this post disappears! #TheRealHistory

rows: حروف كابيتال وعلامات تعجب علشان تستفزك.
Every historian … nobody dares … PROVES everything
كلام مطلق من غير دليل. «صورة واحدة بتثبت كل حاجة» مستحيل.
بيضغط عليك تنشر بسرعة قبل ما تفكر.
صورة واحدة من غير ما يقول هي فين أو مين صوّرها.
THEY LIED … nobody dares to say it
بيوهمك إن فيه حد بيخبي الحقيقة.
حساب مجهول، مش عالم آثار ولا متحف. والـ 2.4M متابع مش دليل.

blocks.text: **الحكم (Fact-check rating):** **Unreliable / misleading.** وفي الحقيقة، علماء الآثار لقوا مقابر العمال اللي بنوا الأهرامات جنبها في الجيزة، وده دليل حقيقي عكس كلام البوست.

text: Who built the pyramids? Excavations near Giza have uncovered the tombs of workers, as well as bakeries and living areas. According to archaeologists, these finds suggest that thousands of skilled Egyptian labourers worked on the pyramids in organised teams. Read the full research summary on our website.

items.ar: لغة **حذرة** (hedging): suggest مش PROVE. ده علامة على الأمانة العلمية.

blocks.text: إزاي تتأكد قبل ما تعمل Share؟ (5 خطوات)

items: **Stop:** وقف ثانية. لو حسيت إنك اتخضيت أو اتحمست جامد، ده بالظبط اللي البوست عايزه.
**Check the source:** مين صاحب الحساب؟ خبير ولا مجهول؟
**Look for evidence:** فين المصدر؟ دراسة؟ اسم عالم؟ ولا «scientists say» وخلاص؟
**Read laterally:** افتح مواقع تانية موثوقة (جرنال معروف، جهة رسمية، متحف، جامعة) وشوف قالوا إيه.
**Decide:** reliable / unreliable / need more information. ولو مش متأكد **متعملش share**.

blocks.title: أشهر الأخطاء في الإجابة (غلط ← صح)
items: ✗ «The post is unreliable because it is on social media.» ← ✓ لازم تذكر **علامة محددة + مثال من البوست**: «It uses urgency signals such as "Share before this gets deleted".»
✗ «It is reliable because it has 2 million followers.» ← ✓ عدد المتابعين مش دليل على الصدق.
✗ بتكتب اسم العلامة من غير شرح. ← ✓ اسم العلامة + المثال + **ليه** ده بيخليه مش موثوق.
✗ بتخلط بين **emotional** و**absolute**. ← ✓ emotional = مشاعر (shocking!). absolute = كلام مطلق (always / every / 100%).

blocks.title: قالب الإجابة الجاهز
items: **One feature that makes this post unreliable is** [emotional language / urgency signals …].
**For example, the post says** "…".
**This is designed to** [make readers panic / share without thinking / believe without evidence].
**Therefore, I would not trust this post because** … / **Before sharing, we should always** check the source.

blocks.text: الأسئلة في الكتاب بتيجي كده: «Explain two or three features that make the post reliable or unreliable (e.g. emotional language, urgency signals, selective evidence, absolute language).» و«Explain why checking online information is important before sharing it with others.» وكمان سؤال زي: «Is a smartphone video taken by a civilian more or less reliable than a news broadcast? Justify your view.»

text: I made 500,000 LE in ONE WEEK from my phone!!! No experience needed — literally ANYONE can do it. Only 20 places left in my course. Link in bio before the price goes up! #Success

Model answer: One feature that makes this post unreliable is absolute language. For example, it says "literally ANYONE can do it", which is a claim with no evidence or qualification. Another feature is urgency signals: "Only 20 places left" and "before the price goes up" pressure readers to pay quickly without thinking. Therefore, I would not trust this post, especially because the writer is trying to sell a course.

blocks.text: **مثال محلول — JRE (smartphone video vs news broadcast):**

text: Model answer: In my opinion, a smartphone video can be useful but is usually less reliable than a news broadcast on its own. This is because a short clip may show only part of an event, so it can be a form of selective evidence. In contrast, professional news teams are expected to check facts and use several sources. However, the most reliable approach is to compare both, because even a news channel can make mistakes.

blocks.text: **التدريب الأول:** اسم العلامة (Emotional / Absolute / Urgency / Selective evidence / Conspiracy framing).

items.q: 1. "Share this NOW before they delete it!"
items.a: **Urgency signals** — ضغط واستعجال + إيحاء بإن حد هيمسحه.

items.q: 2. "This HEARTBREAKING video will make you cry!!!"
items.a: **Emotional language** — HEARTBREAKING + cry + !!!

items.q: 3. "Every single fishing boat is destroying the ocean."
items.a: **Absolute language** — «Every single» تعميم من غير دليل.

items.q: 4. "The government doesn't want you to know about this cure."
items.a: **Conspiracy framing** — حد بيخبي الحقيقة.

items.q: 5. A post shows one photo of a dry lake and says: "Egypt has lost all its water!"
items.a: **Selective evidence** (+ absolute) — صورة واحدة بتتعمم على البلد كلها.

items.q: 6. "Our new collection is 100% sustainable! Shop guilt-free!"
items.a: **Absolute language** — 100% من غير دليل أو شهادة. وكمان الهدف **بيع** (Shop).

text: SHARKS ARE FINISHED!!! Scientists CONFIRM it is already too late. Every beach in the world will be shark-free by next year. The media is hiding this. SHARE before it's banned!

A study published in a scientific journal reports that some shark populations in open oceans have fallen sharply since the 1970s, mainly because of overfishing. Not all species are affected in the same way, and some protected areas show signs of recovery. Link to the study in the comments.

items.q:
7. Which post is more reliable?
a. Post A, because it has more followers
b. Post B, because it names its evidence and uses careful language
c. Post A, because scientists confirm it
d. Both are equally reliable
items.a: **b** — Post B بيذكر الدراسة وبيقول «some» و«Not all species». (a) المتابعين مش دليل. (c) «Scientists CONFIRM» من غير اسم أي عالم.

items.q: 8. Find an example of conspiracy framing in Post A.
items.a: «**The media is hiding this.**»

items.q: 9. Find an example of absolute language in Post A.
items.a: «**Every beach in the world will be shark-free by next year.**» أو «it is already too late».

items.q: 10. Which words in Post B show careful (hedged) language? Give TWO.
items.a: «**some** shark populations» و«**Not all species** are affected in the same way» (وكمان «mainly»). الكلمات دي بتمنع التعميم.

items.q:
11. State whether the statement is True (T) or False (F). Justify your answer.
Post B gives readers a way to check its information.
items.a: **True** — Justification: «**Link to the study in the comments.**»

items.q:
12. State whether the statement is True (T) or False (F). Justify your answer.
Post A names the scientists who made the discovery.
items.a: **False** — Justification: بيقول بس «**Scientists CONFIRM**» من غير أي اسم أو دراسة.

items.q: 13. Although Post A is unreliable, is the problem it talks about completely false? Explain using Post B.
items.a: No. Post B shows that some shark populations really have fallen because of overfishing. The problem is real, but Post A exaggerates it. — زي ما الكتاب بيقول في Unit 6: «exaggeration can make people distrust real evidence».

items.q:
14. Which of these is the strongest sign that an online source is reliable?
a. It has a blue tick
b. It has thousands of likes
c. Other trusted sources report the same information
d. It uses capital letters
items.a: **c** — لما مصادر موثوقة تانية تقول نفس الكلام (lateral reading). (a) و(b) مش دليل.

items.q:
15. A post says, "Only 3 hours left to buy at this price!" This is an example of ______
a. selective evidence  b. urgency signals  c. conspiracy framing  d. expert opinion
items.a: **b** — ضغط بالوقت.

items.q:
16. "These finds suggest that…" The word *suggest* makes the claim ______
a. more absolute  b. more careful and honest  c. more emotional  d. more urgent
items.a: **b** — hedging = لغة حذرة، علامة على المصداقية.

items.q:
17. The main aim of a post that says "Link in bio to learn my EXACT secret method" is probably to ______
a. inform readers about history
b. sell something to readers
c. warn readers about danger
d. share a scientific study
items.a: **b** — «Link in bio» + «secret method» = عايز يبيعلك كورس أو منتج.

items.q: 18. Explain TWO features that make this post unreliable: "UNBELIEVABLE!!! The Nile will be completely dry by next summer! One satellite photo PROVES it. The experts are hiding the truth!"
items.a: Model: First, the post uses emotional language, such as "UNBELIEVABLE!!!", to alarm readers instead of informing them. Second, it uses conspiracy framing: "The experts are hiding the truth" suggests that experts are lying, without any evidence. (You could also mention selective evidence: "One satellite photo" is used to prove a huge claim.) Therefore, the post is unreliable.

items.q: 19. Rewrite this post so that it is reliable: "Drinking coffee ALWAYS ruins teenagers' sleep!!! Share NOW!"
items.a: Model: "According to sleep experts, drinking too much caffeine in the evening may make it harder for some teenagers to fall asleep. Try to avoid coffee after 4 p.m. Source: a national health website." — شلنا الكلام المطلق والاستعجال، وزودنا مصدر ولغة حذرة (may / some).

items.q: 20. Why is it important to check online information before sharing it? Give TWO reasons.
items.a: Model: Firstly, sharing false information can spread fear or harm people, for example by making them buy useless products. Secondly, when exaggerated posts spread, people may stop trusting real evidence about serious problems such as climate change.

items.q: 21. A fashion brand posts: "Our clothes are 100% eco-friendly!" What TWO questions should you ask before believing it?
items.a: Model: 1) What evidence or certificate shows that the clothes are eco-friendly? 2) Why is the brand posting this — to inform me or to make me buy more? — أسئلة **What evidence?** و**Why?** من جدول المصدر.

items.q: 22. Is a post by an official museum account always more reliable than a post by an ordinary visitor? Justify your view.
items.a: Model: An official museum account is usually more reliable, but not always (J). This is because a museum has experts and is responsible for what it publishes, while a visitor may not check facts (R). For example, the museum post in this lesson names archaeologists and uses careful language such as "suggest" (E). However, an ordinary visitor can also share useful first-hand photos, and even an official account can make mistakes, so it is still wise to compare sources. — Justify + Reasoning + Evidence + الجانب التاني.

blocks.title: ملخص الدرس في سطرين
items: علامات البوست المضلل (جدول الكتاب): **Emotional language – Absolute language – Urgency signals – Selective evidence – Conspiracy framing**.
اسأل عن المصدر: **Who? What evidence? When? Why? Who else says it?**
**اللايكات والمتابعين والعلامة الزرقا** مش دليل على الصدق.
المصدر الموثوق بيذكر **دليل** ويستخدم لغة **حذرة** (may / suggest / some) ويديك طريقة تتأكد بيها.
في الإجابة: **اسم العلامة + مثال من البوست + ليه بتقلل المصداقية**، وبعدين حكمك.
